sentences.text: Yeneen is a titanosaur sauropod dinosaur genus that includes only the species Yeneen houssayi.
The generic name Yeneen derives from a Tehuelche word meaning cold or winter weather.
The specific epithet houssayi honors Nobel laureate Bernardo Alberto Houssay.
The type locality of Yeneen is the Bajo de la Carpa Formation in Argentina.
Yeneen is known from at least one partial skeleton.
A third specimen, MAU-Pv-LI-731, consists of disarticulated axial and appendicular bones but has not yet been assigned to Yeneen houssayi.
Other titanosaurs from the same formation include Bonitasaura, Inawentu, Overosaurus, Rinconsaurus, and Traukutitan.
The Paleobiology Database records a single fossil occurrence of Yeneen.
Phylogenetic analysis places Yeneen within Saltasauroidea, in a subgroup called "Clade A", diverging after Narambuenatitan and before Overosaurus.
Yeneen lived during the Late Cretaceous Santonian age, approximately 85.7 to 83.6 million years ago.
Its environment was a semi-arid setting influenced by both river (fluvial) and wind-driven (aeolian) processes.
